summary: The harness, scorer, budget guard and holdout isolation are sound, and the unmet items are disclosed honestly and match what I re-measured. The one blocker is that the plan does not actually schedule their resolution. live-eval owns the three tuning files, but none of its acceptance criteria requires the two todo tests to become hard assertions or the miss thresholds to be met.

criteria.description: Scorer correctness and determinism (pure, no model judge; M1/M2/M3/M4 definitions, Wilson intervals, worst-rep slack)
Budget guard (run cap, total cap, failed-call upper bound, 8 full-tune cap, holdout cap logged before the run)
Holdout isolation (manifest hash-checked before any holdout parse, holdout only loaded with --holdout, 3 reps required, per-provider cap of 2)
Unmet items honestly disclosed and thresholds not weakened (fallback M2 47.5%, holdout M1c 3.07%, live M4 8/10)
Plan truly schedules resolution of the unmet items

findings.title: live-eval acceptance criteria do not enforce resolution of the todo misses
findings.detail: The task live-eval (phase release) owns src/ai/fallback.js, src/ai/prompt.js, src/verify/stopwords.js and tuning-log.md, so the owner and files are right. However, its criteria only say 'fallback-tune and determinism tests pass' and 'M1b 100% and M1c <=2% re-run and reported'. A node:test todo passes trivially, so the task could finish with M2 at 47.5% and the todo still in place. Removing the todo exists only as a code comment. The holdout M1c miss (3.07%) has no criterion at all; the only M1c criterion is the tune-set run, which already passes at 1.63%. The release phase says only 'reported against fixed thresholds', which allows a miss to be reported without being fixed or accepted.
findings.recommendation: Amend the live-eval criteria and re-validate the plan. (a) The todo in test/eval/fallback-tune.test.js is removed and the M2 >=60% assertion passes, or the miss is recorded as an open risk (D10) with a user decision on the threshold. (b) The same applies to the holdout M1c todo in test/eval/m1b-m1c.test.js. Any improvement for (b) must be derived only from the tune set and verifier corpus and logged in eval/tuning-log.md. (c) After the last tuning change, re-run the holdout verifier eval once and report the result as measured. Resolved when the amended plan passes plan validation and the plan gate is re-approved.

findings.title: Holdout verifier run exposes failing holdout item ids to the future tuner
findings.detail: The verifier-only holdout eval prints the ids and reason codes of holdout false flags (hold-03, hold-07, hold-11). The tuner owns the verifier files and could be steered by them, which weakens the spec 5.5 rule against tuning on holdout. The manifest check cannot detect this because it guards file bytes only.
findings.recommendation: Print only aggregate counts for holdout verifier runs, or have the live-eval tuning-log entries state that no holdout item was consulted. Optional before the release phase.

findings.title: Verifier misses 4 of 6 out-of-scope fabrication kinds
findings.detail: The probes are reported and not asserted (2/6 flagged). This is disclosed in the submission, and M1b is 63/63 only over the seeded kinds, so 100% M1b should not be read as general coverage.
findings.recommendation: List the gap under open risks (D10) in the release README.

findings.title: Agent-spend cap of USD 8 is plan-level, not harness-enforced
findings.detail: eval/thresholds.json enforces the USD 3 run cap and USD 40 total cap. The tighter USD 8 and USD 1.5 per-run limits and the 3 tune-run cap in live-eval rely on the executor's discipline, since the harness allows 8 full tune runs.
findings.recommendation: Pass --max-cost 1.5 on every live-eval run; no change required.
